item.title: Draft Cabinet Order and Ministerial Ordinance amendments to local-government fee standards
item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications announced a public consultation on 2026-11-12 on draft amendments to local-government fee standards, reflecting changes in prices, labor costs and administrative work. Documented proposals include raising childcare worker examination fees from JPY 12,700 to JPY 13,800, childcare worker registration screening fees from JPY 4,200 to JPY 6,100, and administrative scrivener examination fees from JPY 10,400 to JPY 12,000. The draft Ministerial Ordinance would raise photograph replacement fees for hazardous materials handler and fire protection equipment officer licenses from JPY 1,600 to JPY 1,800. Cabinet approval of the draft Cabinet Order is planned for late December 2026, with commencement planned for 2027-04-01, except amendments concerning those two licenses and the fire protection equipment officer examination, planned for 2027-05-01, and the administrative scrivener examination, planned for 2028-04-01. The draft Ministerial Ordinance would commence on 2027-05-01; the supplied material does not state a comment deadline. item.title: Draft Notice Amendment on Forest-Absorption J-Credits for Greenhouse Gas Reporting
item.description: AI summary: The proposed Notice amendment would add an entity's own efforts to preserve and enhance greenhouse gas absorption through forest management and conservation to the J-Credit scheme definition in item 4 of the domestic certified emission reductions notice. It would amend Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry and Ministry of the Environment Notice No. 3 of March 2010, supporting reporting by specified emitters under the Act on Promotion of Global Warming Countermeasures (Act No. 117 of 1998). The explanatory document states that related instruments already provide for using forest-absorption credits from an entity's own efforts to adjust its own adjusted emissions; this draft would align the credit-definition notice with those provisions. The Ministry of the Environment and Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry published the draft for public comment on 2026-11-12, with a stated deadline of 2026-12-12 00:00 JST. Issuance of the Notice is planned for January 2027, with application planned from April 1, 2027; these are proposed dates, not confirmed implementation. item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of the Environment and the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry proposed amending their Notice No. 2 of 2025 on greenhouse gas reporting calculation methods. The draft would expand the definition of making domestic certified emission reductions non-transferable for emissions adjustment to include credits from a reporting entity's own forest management and conservation activities that preserve or enhance greenhouse gas absorption; the definition also covers other parties' emission-reduction activities. It concerns specified emitters reporting under the Act on Promotion of Global Warming Countermeasures, Act No. 117 of 1998, and Articles 4(5) and 13(3) of the greenhouse gas emissions reporting Ministerial Ordinance. The draft was published for public comment on 2026-11-12, with a stated deadline of 2026-12-12 00:00 JST. item.title: Draft Ministerial Ordinance on Identity Checks for Voluntary My Number Account Management
item.description: AI summary: The proposed Ministerial Ordinance would amend the enforcement regulations for the Act on Management of Deposit and Savings Accounts Using Individual Numbers Based on Depositors' Wishes, revising identity checks by financial institutions and similar entities. For individuals attending in person, the draft would generally require chip-reading for chip-equipped identification and non-forwardable mailing for specified other documents; it would retain the existing photo-ID method for short-stay foreign nationals, diplomats and others for whom the revised methods are difficult. For remote checks, it would abolish specified methods using photographed ID images or mailed copies, retain a route using original anti-forgery documents, and preserve specified alternatives for nonresident foreign nationals and others; mailed corporate identification would generally require originals, with copies still permitted for foreign corporations. The Digital Agency's Digital Society Common Functions Group published the draft for public comment on 2026-11-12, with a stated deadline of 2026-12-12 00:00 JST. The explanatory document states a proposed commencement date of April 1, 2027; this is a draft, not a confirmed enacted change. item.title: Draft Digital Agency Ordinance Revising Identity Checks for Public-Benefit Account Registration
item.description: AI summary: The Digital Agency published a draft amending ordinance for public comment on 2026-11-12, with a stated deadline of 2026-12-12 00:00 JST and proposed commencement on 2027-04-01. It would amend the implementing rules (Digital Agency Ordinance No. 10 of 2021) under Article 18 of the Act on Registration of Deposit and Savings Accounts for Prompt and Reliable Implementation of Public Benefit Payments (Act No. 38 of 2021). For financial institutions and similar entities verifying individual depositors in person, the proposal would require reading chip data when chip-equipped identification is presented; identification without a photograph would also require sending application-related documents by non-forwardable mail or equivalent, while non-chip identification would require such mailing and, if without a photograph, anti-forgery safeguards. For remote verification, it would abolish methods based on identification images photographed using institution-provided software or submitted identification copies, while retaining methods involving original anti-forgery-protected documents for depositors without chip-equipped identification and preserving specified alternatives for depositors who have moved overseas. The listed responsible office is the Digital Agency, Digital Society Common Functions Group. item.title: FSA publishes study-group discussion summary on digital and decentralized finance
item.description: AI summary: The Financial Services Agency published a summary on 2026-11-12 of the first meeting in administrative year 2026 of its Study Group on Approaches to Digital and Decentralized Finance.
